basis: Corticospinal and cerebral white-matter disease defines SPG63. Frequent muscle atrophy (30-79%) reflects neurologic dysfunction, without evidence of a separate muscle lesion.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%) but is secondary to neurologic dysfunction; direct myopathic damage is not established.

basis: This spindle-cell neoplasm typically originates in dermis or subcutis. Neural differentiation does not establish nerve origin; generic connective-tissue ancestry does not establish muscle disease.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the tumor typically arises in dermis or subcutaneous tissue, both covered by this axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: connective-tissue ancestry alone does not establish origin in locomotor connective tissue; muscle involvement is not established as usual.

basis: Hereditary amyloid-processing disease, classified under inborn errors of metabolism, with defining deposition in brain parenchyma and cerebral vessel walls.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the record identifies a hereditary amyloid-processing disorder within inborn errors of metabolism; the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Crush-related skeletal muscle necrosis, acute renal failure and major circulatory shock define the syndrome.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: major circulatory shock is explicitly defining cardiovascular failure; primary labeling does not require a structural heart lesion.

basis: Brain, eye and renal defects define syndrome; intestinal malrotation 2/3. Pituitary failure and hearing loss each 1/1, and skeletal findings, omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intestinal malrotation in 2/3 assessed patients is direct congenital intestinal pathology, with stronger replication than the endocrine findings.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none under cap: pituitary hormone failure is reported in 1/1; retain defining brain/eye/kidney disease and intestinal malrotation documented in 2/3.

basis: PGAM2 deficiency is a muscle glycolytic disorder. Hemolysis in the definition conflicts with its usual phenotype and supplied HPO; acute kidney injury occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.haematologic: none: hemolytic anemia is not characteristic of muscle-specific PGAM2 deficiency and is unsupported by HPO; the supplied definition appears erroneous.

basis: Neurodevelopmental and congenital skeletal phenotype; strabismus 3/7. Macrodontia 4/4 lacks documented functional injury; reflux 1/1 is sparse. VSD 3/17 is below 30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: macrodontia 4/4 does not itself establish functional damage; reflux reported in 1/1 does not establish common direct GI injury in this subtype.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital limb/skeletal malformations belong to the inherited CdLS phenotype; hip dysplasia and scoliosis are each reported in 2/2.

basis: Intellectual disability defines syndrome. Myopia 6/12 and strabismus 4/12 support ocular involvement; congenital heart defects affect about half. Hearing impairment 3/12 is below 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects collectively affect about half of reported CDK8 cases; individual HPO lesion frequencies should not be summed because they can overlap.

basis: Testicular reproductive neoplasm presenting as a mass. Clinically relevant hormonal dysfunction is neither defining nor established as common.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: Sertoli-cell hormone secretion alone does not make this mass-defined reproductive tumor an endocrine disorder; a defining hormonal phenotype is absent.

basis: Lysosomal lipid storage with defining hepatic injury. Splenomegaly alone does not prove dysfunction; hypersplenism/cytopenias are each reported in 1/1. Arteriosclerosis is a separate disease.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly is common, but functional hypersplenism/cytopenias are supported only by isolated 1/1 reports; impairment in at least 30% is not established.
